mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

items.crowdNote: Stocktwits has no sentiment stream for FINN. It holds growth and tech names, so it tends to follow the Nasdaq mood above.

trending.note: Board as of Saturday 4:05 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-20 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: Halozyme Therapeutics Inc.
items.about: Halozyme licenses its ENHANZE technology, which lets drugs normally given by IV be delivered as quick under-the-skin injections.
items.why: A German appeals court on Nov 19 lifted the preliminary injunction that had blocked Merck's under-the-skin Keytruda SC in Germany, a setback for Halozyme's patent case; the company says it will file a full infringement suit seeking permanent relief. The stock fell another 1.8% Friday to a more-than-3-month low, though a separate October Dutch ruling against Merck in eight countries still stands. Posts cite HC Wainwright keeping a Buy rating and $130 target on Nov 20.

items.name: Johnson & Johnson
items.about: Johnson & Johnson develops and sells prescription medicines and medical devices.
items.why: J&J rose 1.2% on a day the Nasdaq fell about 5%, and posts describe money moving into defensive healthcare names. After the close, Fierce Pharma reported that the FDA had rebuked J&J over promotional claims about the bladder-sparing benefits of its bladder-cancer drug Inlexzo. Posts also mention J&J as a possible bidder for SELLAS (SLS) after its Phase 3 readout, which is unconfirmed speculation.

items.name: Natera Inc
items.about: Natera runs cell-free DNA tests for prenatal screening, organ transplant monitoring and cancer recurrence.
items.why: Natera fell 5.7% Friday, adding to a November slide. The stock dropped 14.6% after Q3 results on Nov 5, and a sudden CEO transition weighed on it again on Nov 16, when Trefis had it down about 24% for the month. Posts also note Natera will run ctDNA testing on the remaining patients in CytoDyn's trial.

items.name: Grayscale Ethereum Mini Trust
items.about: An exchange-traded trust that holds ether, so investors can follow the Ethereum token's price from a brokerage account.
items.why: The trust fell 9.1% Friday as ether broke below the $1,600 support level during the broad risk-off selloff. Stocktwits News reported that Peter Schiff warned ether could reach $1,000 by Monday. Saturday posts show ether bouncing about 3% to roughly $1,685.

items.name: Sony Group Corporation
items.about: Sony makes PlayStation consoles and games, image sensors and electronics, and owns music and film studios.
items.why: Sony edged up 0.3% on a down day. Posts linked IGN's report that GTA 6 sold $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours, which they expect to lift PlayStation demand. Sony had already raised its full-year operating profit forecast to ¥1.87 trillion, and posts citing Bloomberg say it pulled out of talks to anchor a new Hudson Yards office tower.

items.name: Jersey Mike's Subs Inc.
items.about: Jersey Mike's franchises a chain of sub sandwich shops.
items.why: Jersey Mike's, a recent listing with only a few months of trading history, fell 4.7% to close near the day's low under $17. Posts say it now trades well below the roughly $21 seen in its early days, and holders discussed its first $0.35 dividend and plans to expand in Europe. No company news was cited for Friday's drop.

items.name: Delcath Systems Inc
items.about: Delcath makes the Hepzato system, which delivers high-dose chemotherapy directly to the liver for cancers that have spread there.
items.why: Delcath slipped 2.3% Friday and to $18.50 after hours. Chatter centered on the UK after NICE published guidance on chemosaturation for ocular melanoma that has spread to the liver; NHS bodies usually have about 90 days to fund a recommended treatment. Posts estimate the UK revenue upside, which the company has not quantified.

items.name: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. Class A
items.about: Berkshire Hathaway is Warren Buffett's former conglomerate, owning insurers, BNSF railroad, utilities and a large stock portfolio.
items.why: Berkshire's Class A shares fell only 0.5% while the Nasdaq dropped about 5%, and chatter hit extremely high. Posts speculate the company's large cash pile could be put to work in the selloff, with some naming Nvidia. No Berkshire announcement was cited.

items.name: SPDR S&P Biotech ETF
items.about: An equal-weighted ETF of US biotechnology stocks.
items.why: The biotech ETF fell 2.7% with the broader market, and posts say it closed below its 50-day average. Much of the talk was about SELLAS (SLS), whose Phase 3 REGAL leukemia data drew buyout speculation, and about Stanley Druckenmiller's new biotech positions in his Q3 13F filing.

items.name: Vale S.A.
items.about: Vale is a Brazilian miner and one of the world's largest producers of iron ore and nickel.
items.why: Vale fell 3.5% to a new 52-week low. Posts say Brazil's home market was closed for a holiday, so only the US-listed shares traded, and they blame weaker iron ore and the Brazilian real. Holders cite a dividend yield near 10% and say the stock is down about 23% this year.

items.name: CVS Health Corp
items.about: CVS runs pharmacies, the Caremark pharmacy-benefit business and the Aetna health insurer.
items.why: CVS gained 1% as health insurers held up during the selloff. After the close, posts say CMS proposed changes to how Medicare Advantage Star Ratings are calculated, and insurers fell about 2% after hours, with CVS trading near $79.60. Posters disagree on whether the change helps or hurts Aetna.

items.name: Novo Nordisk A/S
items.about: Novo Nordisk is a Danish drugmaker best known for the diabetes and obesity drugs Ozempic and Wegovy.
items.why: Novo fell 2.7% toward a multi-year low, and posts note it tracked the market down instead of acting like a defensive drug stock. Holders point to forced US price cuts on its GLP-1 drugs and say it has to show growth before big buyers return. No new company news was linked on Friday.

items.name: Zscaler Inc
items.about: Zscaler sells cloud-based security that inspects and protects company internet and app traffic.
items.why: Zscaler closed down 5.3% in the selloff, then jumped about 16–20% after hours to around $226 after Bloomberg and Reuters reported that CrowdStrike is in talks to buy it. No deal or price has been announced, and Bloomberg framed the talks as AI-driven consolidation in cybersecurity. CrowdStrike reports on Dec 1 and Zscaler on Dec 2.

items.name: Altria Group Inc.
items.about: Altria sells Marlboro cigarettes and other tobacco and nicotine products in the US.
items.why: Altria edged up 0.3% while the Nasdaq fell about 5%. Posts called it the only green in their portfolios as money moved into defensive dividend payers. Posts also note tobacco stocks were still down 4–7% since Monday without company news.

items.name: Lufax Holding Ltd ADR
items.about: Lufax is a Chinese consumer and small-business lending platform backed by Ping An.
items.why: Lufax slid 1.8% to close at the day's low of $5.95, which posts call a new low, as China fintech stocks stayed weak. Holders are debating a possible take-private offer and how far the stock trades below book value. No company news was cited.

items.name: CAVA Group Inc
items.about: CAVA runs a chain of fast-casual Mediterranean restaurants.
items.why: CAVA fell 4.7% to just under $49, closing near the day's low. Posts say it is down about 17% since Nov 6. Bearish posts blame a weak last earnings report and the break below $50 as growth restaurant stocks sold off with the market.

items.name: Core Scientific Inc
items.about: Core Scientific runs large data centers that host bitcoin mining and AI computing for customers like CoreWeave.
items.why: Core Scientific dropped 15.2% as AI data-center stocks sold off, part of a slide that deepened after Anthropic's IPO on Nov 19 failed to revive the AI trade. Posts link a CNBC report that President Trump threatened a heavy tax on US companies building data centers abroad, which I could not confirm. Posters also say high funding costs are weighing on leveraged hosting balance sheets.

items.name: Merck & Co Inc
items.about: Merck is a global drugmaker whose top product is the cancer immunotherapy Keytruda.
items.why: Merck rose 0.7% after a German appeals court on Nov 19 lifted the injunction that had blocked Keytruda SC in Germany, a win in its patent fight with Halozyme. Much of the chatter comes from SELLAS (SLS) holders speculating, without confirmation, that Merck could bid for the company after its Phase 3 leukemia data. Posts also say Merck dropped its own Phase 3 blood-cancer drug on Nov 17.

items.name: iShares MSCI Brazil ETF
items.about: An ETF that holds large and mid-sized Brazilian companies such as Petrobras, Vale and Itaú.
items.why: The Brazil ETF fell 3.3% Friday, and posts say it lost about 10% for the week compared with a 3.5% weekly drop for the Ibovespa. Brazil's own market was closed for a holiday on Friday, so the US-listed fund traded alone. Posts blame the falling real and weaker iron ore.

items.name: Legend Biotech
items.about: Legend Biotech develops cell therapies, including the multiple myeloma CAR-T treatment Carvykti partnered with J&J.
items.why: Legend fell 5.3% to another 52-week low as biotech stocks sold off. Posts cite a filing showing the CEO bought about $163,000 of shares on Nov 17. Holders also point to cautious 2027 guidance and expect tax-loss selling into December.
